append.text: **Ps 7:18, a place the coordinator named:** *Darei graças ao Senhor segundo a sua justiça* — holds (MS1932 *Glorificarei*, DRB *give glory*); passed the Latinist twice, no remark from the stylist or the blind reader.

**Ps 7:7b, its second place:** *levantai-vos, Senhor, meu Deus, no decreto que mandastes* — holds: a judicial word in a judicial psalm; the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard "rise to carry out / in keeping with the decree"; the stylist asked for *preceito*, refused under D19.

**Ps 7:7b *in præcépto quod mandásti*:** a noun object, which *dar ordem* cannot take → *no decreto que mandastes* (the row's first alternative, *mandar*, of one family with *mandamentos*). The stylist heard *mandar um decreto* as sending it and asked for *ordenastes* (option there, and the Ps 2 agent's trial wording); the blind reader heard "o decreto que emitistes". Three candidates now — *dar ordem*, *mandar*, *ordenar* — wants a ruling; 12 verses (grep: 7:7b, 32:9, 41:9, 77:5, 77:23, 90:11, 104:8, 110:9a, 118:4, 118:138, 132:3b, 148:5).

**Ps 7:6: *calque* failed two readers** — the stylist ("pouco corrente") and the blind reader (unknown word) — so Ps 7 has *pise aos pés na terra a minha vida*: this row's plainer verb with *aos pés* kept, because bare *pise na terra* is heard as treading the earth. Proposed for the row: *pisar aos pés*; Ps 90:13 still has *calcar*.
**Ps 7:10, the verse this row names:** *Deus, vós que sondais os corações e os rins* — holds; no reader remarked on the verb.

**Ps 7:10 *díriges justum* → *e dirigireis o justo*:** a future, which the ban does not reach; with a person as object it says "guide, steer" (DRB *direct*). Passed all three readers; options *encaminhareis* (MS1932), *endireitareis*.

**Ps 7:13, 7:17:** the verb twice — *Se não vos voltardes … A sua dor se voltará sobre a sua cabeça* — one verb for the echo (the turn refused is the turn suffered). In 7:13 conversion *is* the sense, MS1932 and DRB have the cognate, and the blind reader found **a cost of *vós*: *Se não vos voltardes* can be heard as said to God** (whom 6:5 asks *Voltai-vos*), which the Latin's plural excludes; he heard repentance first, and *ele brandirá* corrects it at once. *Converterdes* is option 2 there — for Gustavo's ear.

**Ps 7:6 meets another build:** *glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat* (an enemy brings a man's glory down into the dust; 21:16 *in púlverem mortis deduxísti me* is the same) → *faça descer ao pó a minha glória* (L&S "lead or bring down", DRB). *Guie ao pó* makes the enemy a kindly guide. D22 stands for *deduc me*.

**Ps 7:5 *décidam … ab inimícis meis*: *cair de* fails with persons** ("caia eu dos meus inimigos" says nothing) → *caia eu vazio, com razão, diante dos meus inimigos* (DRB *before*). **Stands against the Latinist (major, twice)**, who reads the agent only and wants *por obra dos*: refused because the Latin calques ἀποπέσοιν ἀπό (separation) and is open, neither Vulgate-family version has an agent, and the blind reader heard "defeated by the enemies" first.
Ps 7:7a, 7:7b *Levantai-vos, Senhor … E levantai-vos, Senhor, meu Deus* — applied twice; no reader remarked.
Ps 7:9b *Julgai-me, Senhor, segundo a minha justiça* (= 25:1's opening), 7:8b *o Senhor julga os povos* — here the sense is plainly "do me justice"; no reader heard condemnation.

Ps 7:18 = 12:6b *nómini Dómini altíssimi* → *ao nome do altíssimo Senhor*: the adjective moved before the noun at the stylist's request, so that the verse closes on an oxytone (the word is a proparoxytone; Ps 90:1 lets it stand at a mediant).
Ps 7:11 *Justo é o meu auxílio vindo do Senhor* — the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's shield; the blind reader heard "the help is just" before "the helper is just".
Ps 7:2 *em vós esperei*: the blind reader heard hope first, waiting second.

terms: | redímere | resgatar (*enquanto não há quem resgate, nem quem salve*) | open | Ps 7:3; λυτρόομαι; 12 verses with the present stem (grep: 7:3, 25:11, 33:23, 43:26, 48:8, 48:16, 54:19, 71:14, 102:4, 118:134, 118:154, 129:8) and 9 with the perfect (30:6 *redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis* — the verse of *In manus tuas*; 70:23, 73:2, 76:15, 77:42, 105:10, 106:2, 135:24, 143:10): *resgatastes-me* must be weighed there against *remir* (*vós me remistes* — the traditional verb, from memory, unverified). The cognate fails at the four imperatives: *redimi-me* is also "I redeemed myself" (D13's test) — *resgatai-me*, *resgatai-nos* are safe. The noun *redémptio* (110:9a, 129:7) can stay *redenção*. MS1932 *livrar* is *liberáre*'s |
| rápere | arrebatar | working | Ps 7:3 *Para que não arrebate a minha alma como um leão* (MS1932); 9:30b, 21:14 *leo rápiens*, 49:22, 103:21; apart from *erípere* |

| réddere | pagar (*Se paguei aos que me retribuíam males*) | open | Ps 7:5 (MS1932's verb), beside *retribúere* → retribuir — the Greek has one verb twice, the Latin two; will serve *vota réddere* (*pagarei os meus votos*, 21:26, 49:14, 55:12, 60:9, 65:13, 115:5, 115:9 — grep) and *redde retributiónem* (27:4, 93:2); *pagai* is safe |

| comprehéndere | prender (*e a prenda*) | open | Ps 7:6; 7 verses (grep: 7:6, 9:23, 17:38, 39:13, 58:13, 68:25, 70:11), twice after *pérsequi* (17:38, 70:11). The Latin verb's own descendant, "lay hold of"; tried in each: *são presos nos conselhos*, *as minhas iniquidades me prenderam*, *sejam presos na sua soberba*, *o furor da vossa ira os prenda*. The Greek's "overtake" (καταλαμβάνω) is not heard — option *alcançar*; MS1932 *apoderar-se de*. Passed all three readers |
| pérsequi | perseguir | working | Ps 7:2, 7:6; 16 verses. **Rule-3 trap ahead: 70:11 *persequímini* → bare *persegui* is also "I pursued"** |
| inánis | vazio | working | Ps 7:5 (DRB *empty*); 106:9 *ánimam inánem*; the blind reader heard "stripped of everything". *inánia* (2:1) is *coisas vãs* |

| *Exaltáre* (passive imperative, to God) | *exaltai-vos* | open | Ps 7:7a *e exaltai-vos nos confins dos meus inimigos*; the form opens 20:14, 56:6, 56:12, 93:2, 107:6 (*Exaltáre super cælos, Deus* → *Exaltai-vos acima dos céus, Deus*). The pronominal form for a medio-passive, matching *Levantai-vos* as ὑψώθητι matches ἀνάστηθι; safe (past *exaltei*). The Latinist passed it twice. Option *sede exaltado* (DRB), the passive to the letter |

| fines (of a people) | confins | open | Ps 7:7a *nos confins dos meus inimigos* (DRB *borders*) — the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's "rage"; both the edges and the lands; the blind reader listed *confins* as unknown and still heard "in their lands". Goes with *fines terræ* → os confins da terra |

| synagóga | congregação (*e a congregação dos povos vos cercará*) | open | Ps 7:7b; 4 verses (grep: 7:7b, 81:1 *in synagóga deórum*, 85:14 *synagóga poténtium*, 105:18). The cognate is a building. Shares the word with *congregátio* (5 verses) on D15's test: in 105:17–18, where the two stand in neighbouring verses, the Greek has συναγωγή both times (read in `consult/parallels/ps105.md`). Keeps *assembleia* out of a third collision (*concílium*, *ecclésia*). **Heard by the blind reader first as a religious community**; options *assembleia* (the right word for 81:1), *ajuntamento* |
| régredi | regressar (*regressai ao alto*) | working | Ps 7:8b, only here; leaves *voltar* to *convértere*; the blind reader heard "return to heaven" first |
| nequítia | maldade | open | Ps 7:10 *Será consumida a maldade dos pecadores*; 4 verses (27:4, 54:16, 72:8 beside *iniquitátem*); leaves *malícia* to *malítia* (7 verses); MS1932 *malícia* |

| renes | rins | open | Ps 7:10 *os corações e os rins*; 15:7, 25:2 *ure renes meos et cor meum*, 72:21, 138:13 — the organ named (rule 5); the blind reader heard the inmost feelings first and noted it can be taken literally; MS1932 *entranhas* |

| numquid | acaso | open | Ps 7:12 *acaso se ira todos os dias?* — the Latin's reading (a patient judge), against the Hebrew's; 14 verses, five running in Ps 87; the blind reader heard the expected "no" first; MS1932 *porventura* |
| per síngulos dies | todos os dias | working | Ps 7:12; 41:11, 144:2; as Ps 6:7 *per síngulas noctes* → todas as noites |
| judex / fortis / pátiens | juiz / forte / paciente | working | Ps 7:12; *pátiens* 85:15, 144:8 (μακρόθυμος) |

| vibráre | brandir (*ele brandirá a sua espada*) | working | Ps 7:13, only here; *vibrará a sua espada* is heard as the sword vibrating; the blind reader listed *brandirá* as unknown but paraphrased it rightly; option *agitará* |

| téndere / inténdere arcum | armar o arco | open | Ps 7:13 *armou o seu arco, e o preparou* (MS1932); *inténdere arcum* 10:3, 36:14, 57:8, 63:4, 77:9 cannot take *inténdere* → atender; exact but little-known option *retesar* |
| vasa (plural) | instrumentos | open | Ps 7:14 *instrumentos de morte* (DRB); 70:22 *in vasis psalmi*; the singular stays *vaso* (2:9, 30:13) |
| sagítta | seta | working | Ps 90:6, Ps 7:14; 14 verses |

| parturíre / párere | sentir as dores de parto de / dar à luz | open | Ps 7:15 *Eis que sentiu as dores de parto da injustiça: concebeu a dor, e deu à luz a iniquidade* — three verbs kept three, in the Latin's odd order. The first is the stylist's (draft 1 *esteve de parto da* "sounds translated"); cost: *dores* one colon before *a dor*. *Pariu* is the concrete option for *péperit*. 47:7 *dolóres ut parturiéntis* |
| dolor | dor | working | Ps 7:15, 7:17 |

| lacus / fóvea | cova / fosso | open | Ps 7:16 *Abriu uma cova, e a cavou: e caiu no fosso que fez*. *lacus* 7 verses, four of them *descendéntibus in lacum* (27:1, 29:4, 87:5, 142:7b) → *os que descem à cova*; 39:3 *de lacu misériæ*; *fóvea* 56:7 (a near twin: *Cavaram um fosso diante de mim, e caíram nele*), 93:13. *effódere* (only here) shares *cavar* with *fódere* |

| vertex | o alto da cabeça | open | Ps 7:17 *e sobre o alto da sua cabeça descerá a sua iniquidade* — the Latinist's fix for draft 1 *crânio* (the bone); says *cabeça* twice where the Latin has *caput … vérticem*; 67:22 *vérticem capílli* |

| psállere | entoar salmos (*e entoarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor*) | open | Ps 7:18 = 12:6b. **Heavy: everywhere in the psalter** (12 verses have *psallam* alone). Stands in one verse with *cantáre* (12:6b, 20:14, 103:33, 107:2), so the verb cannot be *cantar*: the stylist's *cantarei salmos* would give *cantarei … cantarei* in 12:6b. Draft 1 had the cognate *salmodiarei* (one word for one): heavy and specialised for the stylist, unknown to the blind reader. *Entoar salmos* keeps the dative, is safe at the imperative (*entoai salmos*; 46:7 has *psállite* four times), and the Latinist passed it. Cost: two words for one; beside *psalmum dícere* the noun will be shared. Wants a ruling before Ps 9 |
| rectus corde | reto de coração | working | Ps 7:11 *que salva os retos de coração*; 10:3, 31:11, 36:14, 63:11, 96:11, 124:4 |
| innocéntia | inocência | working | Ps 7:9b; 8 verses |
| mérito | com razão | working | Ps 7:5 (MS1932); only here |
formulas: | *et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi* (7:18b = 12:6b, last colon) | *e entoarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor* | open (hangs on *psállere*) — Ps 7; **Ps 12 copies it** |
| *nequándo rápiat* (7:3, 49:22) | *para que não arrebate* — no subject supplied | working — Ps 7; in 49:22 the one who seizes is God |

| *secúndum innocéntiam meam super me* (7:9b) | *segundo a minha inocência sobre mim* | open — Ps 7; the Septuagintal *super me* (ἐπ᾿ ἐμοί) kept, open between "the innocence that is upon me" and "judge … over me"; MS1932 *que há em mim* is the option |
